plans.title: The Four Gospels in 30 Days
plans.blurb: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, about three chapters a day. A steady pace that finishes in a month.

plans.title: The Gospels, One Chapter a Day
plans.blurb: All 89 chapters, one a day, in Gospel order. Slow and easy to keep up.

plans.title: The Life of Jesus
plans.blurb: Thirty readings from the Gospels in the order of his life: birth, ministry, last week and resurrection.

days.t: Prayer, worry and the narrow gate
Calling Matthew and sending the Twelve
Who do you say I am?
Lost sheep, lost coin, lost son
Zacchaeus and the road to Jerusalem
The empty tomb and the commission

plans.title: Mark in 8 Days
plans.blurb: The shortest Gospel, fast-moving and vivid. Two chapters a day.

plans.title: John in 21 Days
plans.blurb: The Gospel that begins with the Word. One chapter a day.

plans.title: Luke in 24 Days
plans.blurb: The most complete account of his life. One chapter a day.

plans.title: Matthew in 28 Days
plans.blurb: The Gospel that ties Jesus to Israel's story. One chapter a day.

plans.title: The Sermon on the Mount
plans.blurb: Matthew 5 to 7, one chapter a day.

plans.title: Parables of Jesus
plans.blurb: Ten days with the stories Jesus told, one chapter each.

days.t: The persistent widow and the tax collector
Ten bridesmaids, talents, sheep and goats

plans.title: Holy Week in Matthew
plans.blurb: The last week of Jesus' life, Matthew 21 to 28.

days.t: The triumphal entry and the temple

plans.title: The Last Days in John
plans.blurb: John 12 to 21, from the anointing at Bethany to the breakfast on the beach.

plans.title: The Resurrection in Four Gospels
plans.blurb: Four days, four accounts of the empty tomb.

plans.title: Acts in 28 Days
plans.blurb: The whole book of Acts, one chapter a day, from the ascension to Paul in Rome.

plans.title: Acts in 14 Days
plans.blurb: Two chapters a day through the story of the first church.

plans.title: Luke and Acts in 52 Days
plans.blurb: Luke wrote both books. Read his Gospel and then the sequel, one chapter a day.

plans.title: The Church Begins
plans.blurb: Acts 1 to 12: Pentecost, Stephen, Philip, Saul on the Damascus road, Peter and Cornelius.

days.t: The lame man at the Beautiful Gate
Ananias and Sapphira, and the apostles freed
Philip in Samaria and the Ethiopian
Cornelius and the sheet of animals

plans.title: Paul's Journeys
plans.blurb: Twelve days from Antioch to Rome: three missionary journeys, the council, the arrest and the voyage.

days.t: The first journey: Cyprus and Galatia
The second journey: Philippi, Thessalonica, Athens

plans.title: The Speeches of Acts
plans.blurb: Seven sermons and defenses, from Peter at Pentecost to Paul before Agrippa.

plans.title: Romans in 16 Days
plans.blurb: The whole letter, one chapter a day, from Paul's greeting to the final doxology.

plans.title: Romans in 8 Days
plans.blurb: Two chapters a day through the letter that explains the gospel.

plans.title: Romans 1-8: The Good News Explained
plans.blurb: Sin, justification by faith, life in the Spirit and the hope of glory.

days.t: The gospel and the wrath of God
All have sinned, all are justified freely
Dead to sin, alive to God
The law and the divided self

plans.title: Romans 9-11: God and Israel
plans.blurb: Three chapters on God's promises to Israel, the remnant, and the olive tree.

days.t: The remnant and the olive tree

plans.title: Romans 12-16: Living It Out
plans.blurb: A living sacrifice, love, the authorities, the weak and the strong, and Paul's greetings.

days.t: Authorities, love and the coming day
Accept one another, and Paul's plans
Greetings to the church in Rome

plans.title: The Roman Road
plans.blurb: Five chapters that many Christians read in order to follow the argument of the gospel.

days.t: The wages of sin and the gift of God

plans.title: The Story Behind Romans
plans.blurb: Paul in Corinth and Ephesus, the three months in Greece, and the letter he wrote there, ending with his arrival in Rome.

days.t: Paul's plans for Rome and Spain

plans.title: 1 Corinthians in 16 Days
plans.blurb: The whole letter, one chapter a day, from Paul's greeting to the church in Corinth to his closing words.

plans.title: 1 Corinthians in 8 Days
plans.blurb: Two chapters a day through the letter to a gifted and troubled church.

plans.title: 1 Corinthians 1-4: Wisdom and Division
plans.blurb: Quarrels over leaders, the message of the cross, and what it means to be God's building.

days.t: Divisions and the foolishness of the cross
The wisdom that comes by the Spirit
Planted, watered and built on Christ

plans.title: 1 Corinthians 5-7: Life Together
plans.blurb: Discipline, lawsuits, the body, marriage and singleness: how believers live among their neighbors.

days.t: A scandal and the old leaven
Lawsuits and the body as a temple

plans.title: 1 Corinthians 8-11: Freedom and the Table
plans.blurb: Food offered to idols, Paul's rights, warnings from Israel, and the Lord's Supper.

days.t: Rights given up for the gospel

plans.title: 1 Corinthians 12-14: Gifts, Body and Love
plans.blurb: Spiritual gifts, one body with many members, the love chapter, and order in worship.

plans.title: The Story Behind 1 Corinthians
plans.blurb: Paul founds the church in Corinth, settles in Ephesus, and answers the news that reaches him there.

days.t: The collection, Timothy and the plans

plans.title: The Witnesses to the Resurrection
plans.blurb: The four Gospels' accounts of Easter morning, then Paul's earlier list of witnesses and what the resurrection means.

days.t: Matthew: the empty tomb and the great commission
Mark: the young man at the tomb
John: Mary, Thomas and the disciples
Paul: the creed, the witnesses and the new body

plans.title: The Lord's Supper
plans.blurb: The last supper in the four Gospels, and the oldest written account in Paul's letter to Corinth.

days.t: Matthew: the Passover meal and the cup
Mark: the bread and the cup

plans.title: 2 Corinthians in 13 Days
plans.blurb: The whole letter, one chapter a day, from comfort in trouble to the closing blessing.

plans.title: 2 Corinthians in 7 Days
plans.blurb: Two chapters a day through Paul's most personal letter.

plans.title: 2 Corinthians 1-7: Comfort and Reconciliation
plans.blurb: Comfort in suffering, a painful visit, the new covenant, jars of clay and the ministry of reconciliation.

days.t: Forgiveness, Troas and the fragrance of Christ
The new covenant and the veil

plans.title: 2 Corinthians 8-9: The Grace of Giving
plans.blurb: Paul's two chapters on the collection for the saints in Jerusalem.

days.t: The Macedonians, Christ's example and the delegates
Sowing generously and a cheerful giver

plans.title: 2 Corinthians 10-13: Paul Defends His Ministry
plans.blurb: The critics, the super-apostles, the fool's boast, the thorn in the flesh and the third visit.

days.t: The super-apostles and the fool's boast
Visions, the thorn and power in weakness

plans.title: Strength in Weakness
plans.blurb: Four chapters where Paul shows that God's power works through weakness: jars of clay, the marks of a minister, the fool's boast and the thorn.

days.t: My grace is sufficient for you

plans.title: The Story Behind 2 Corinthians
plans.blurb: Paul in Ephesus, the plan to visit, the painful visit and sharp letter, Titus's good news, and the third visit.

days.t: Trouble in Asia and a changed plan
The painful visit and the tearful letter
The thorn and the visit to come

plans.title: Galatians in 6 Days
plans.blurb: The whole letter, one chapter a day, from "a different gospel" to "a new creation."

plans.title: Galatians in 3 Days
plans.blurb: Two chapters a day: Paul's story, the argument from Abraham and the life of freedom.

days.t: Paul's call and the Jerusalem meeting
Abraham, the promise and the law
Freedom, the Spirit and the new creation

plans.title: Paul's Story in Galatians 1-2
plans.blurb: Paul tells how he met Christ, visited Jerusalem and stood up to Peter at Antioch.

days.t: Called by grace and taught by revelation
The pillars, Titus and the confrontation at Antioch

plans.title: Faith, Promise and Freedom
plans.blurb: Three chapters on Abraham, the law as guardian, sons and heirs, Hagar and Sarah, and standing firm in freedom.

days.t: Stand firm and walk by the Spirit

plans.title: The Background to Galatians
plans.blurb: The journey to Pisidian Antioch, Iconium and Lystra and the council in Jerusalem, then the central chapters of the letter. Where and when Galatians was written is debated, so this plan reads the setting first.

days.t: Peter, Paul and the truth of the gospel
Freedom and the fruit of the Spirit

plans.title: Ephesians in 6 Days
plans.blurb: The whole letter, one chapter a day, from "every spiritual blessing" to the armor of God.

plans.title: Ephesians in 3 Days
plans.blurb: Two chapters a day: what God has done in Christ, the mystery and the call to unity, and the life of light, home and armor.

days.t: Blessed in Christ and saved by grace
The mystery, Paul's prayer and the unity of the body
Walking in light, the household and the armor of God

plans.title: Saved by Grace, One in Christ
plans.blurb: Three chapters on God's plan from before the world began, the gift of salvation, the wall between Jew and Gentile torn down, and the prayer for love that fills.

days.t: Dead, made alive, and one new people
The mystery and a prayer for love

plans.title: Walk Worthy of the Calling
plans.blurb: The practical half of the letter: unity and gifts, putting off the old self, children of light, the family and household, and standing in God's armor.

days.t: Imitators of God and children of light
Home, work and the armor of God

plans.title: The Background to Ephesians
plans.blurb: Paul in Ephesus and his farewell to its elders, his time under guard in Rome, then the letter's great chapters. Where Ephesians was written is debated, and Rome is the traditional view.

days.t: Saved by grace and one in Christ
The armor of God and the messenger Tychicus

plans.title: Philippians in 4 Days
plans.blurb: The whole letter, one chapter a day, from "Joy in Chains" to "Rejoice in the Lord always."

plans.title: Philippians in One Sitting
plans.blurb: All four chapters in a single reading. The letter is short, and it was meant to be read aloud to the church in one go.

plans.title: Joy in Chains
plans.blurb: Three chapters on rejoicing while a prisoner: chains that advance the gospel, the humility of Christ, and joy, prayer and contentment.

plans.title: What Paul Counted as Loss
plans.blurb: Paul tells his own story three times: his zeal in Acts 22, his own account in Galatians 1, and the list he gave up in Philippians 3.

days.t: Paul tells the crowd about his past

plans.title: The Background to Philippians
plans.blurb: How the church at Philippi began, the jail and the earthquake, Paul under guard in Rome, then the letter itself. Where Philippians was written is debated, and Rome is the traditional view.

days.t: Lydia and the jailer at Philippi
Thessalonica, where the Philippians sent help

plans.title: Colossians in 4 Days
plans.blurb: The whole letter, one chapter a day, from the image of the invisible God to the greetings at the end.

days.t: The Son, image of the invisible God

plans.title: Colossians in One Sitting
plans.blurb: All four chapters in a single reading. The letter was meant to be read aloud to the church, and then passed on to Laodicea.

plans.title: Who Is Christ?
plans.blurb: Three great passages on who Jesus is: the Word who was with God, the Servant who was exalted, and the Son who is the image of the invisible God.

days.t: The image of the invisible God

plans.title: Raised with Christ
plans.blurb: Buried and raised in baptism, set free from empty rules, and called to put off the old self and put on the new.

days.t: Dead to sin, alive to God
Complete in Christ, free from empty rules
Put off the old self, put on the new

plans.title: The Background to Colossians
plans.blurb: Paul in Ephesus while the word spread through Asia, Paul under guard in Rome, then the letter to a church he had never visited. Where Colossians was written is debated, and Rome is the traditional view.

plans.title: 1 Thessalonians in 5 Days
plans.blurb: The whole letter, one chapter a day: thanks for a young church, Paul's care, Timothy's news, hope for those who have died, and the Day of the Lord.

days.t: A church that turned to God
Like a nursing mother and a father
Holiness, work and those who sleep in death
The Day of the Lord and final words

plans.title: 2 Thessalonians in 3 Days
plans.blurb: The shorter second letter, one chapter a day: endurance under pressure, the Day that has not yet come, and the call to work.

days.t: The Day of the Lord and the man of lawlessness
Pray, work and do not grow weary

plans.title: Both Thessalonian Letters in 8 Days
plans.blurb: Paul's earliest surviving letters, probably written from Corinth, one chapter a day: 1 Thessalonians 1-5, then 2 Thessalonians 1-3.

days.t: A church that turned to God
Like a nursing mother and a father
Holiness, work and those who sleep in death
The Day of the Lord and final words
The Day of the Lord and the man of lawlessness
Pray, work and do not grow weary

plans.title: 1 Thessalonians in One Sitting
plans.blurb: All five chapters at once. The letter was meant to be read aloud to the whole church (5:27), and it takes about fifteen minutes.

plans.title: Hope for Those Who Have Died
plans.blurb: Grief and hope: the resurrection of Jesus, believers who sleep in death, the coming of the Lord and what Paul tells the church to do while they wait.

days.t: Awake, sober and encouraging one another

plans.title: The Day of the Lord
plans.blurb: A thief in the night, a false report that the Day had come, and a warning about the man of lawlessness. Some of the passages are debated.

days.t: Like a thief in the night
The Lord Jesus revealed from heaven

plans.title: Work, Rest and Quiet Lives
plans.blurb: Paul worked night and day among the Thessalonians. Three readings on his example and on the command to work quietly and eat one's own bread.

days.t: Quiet work with your own hands
If anyone is unwilling to work

plans.title: The Story Behind the Thessalonian Letters
plans.blurb: Paul and Silas at Philippi and Thessalonica, the escape to Berea and Athens, Corinth and Timothy's report, and then the two letters. The place of writing is an inference from Acts.

days.t: A second letter to the same church

plans.title: 1 Timothy in 6 Days
plans.blurb: The whole letter, one chapter a day: a charge to stay at Ephesus, prayer and worship, the leaders of the church, false teaching, widows and elders, and the call to guard what has been entrusted.

days.t: Prayer, one mediator and the women in the assembly
Overseers, deacons and the pillar of the truth
Widows, elders and a little wine
Contentment, money and the good fight

plans.title: 1 Timothy in 3 Days
plans.blurb: Two chapters a day through Paul's letter to Timothy at Ephesus.

days.t: The charge and the church at prayer
Leaders and the hymn about Christ, then false teaching
The church as a family, and the final charge

plans.title: 1 Timothy in One Sitting
plans.blurb: All six chapters at once, about twenty minutes. A letter from an older worker to a younger one who has been left with a hard task.

plans.title: Paul, Ephesus and Timothy
plans.blurb: Paul's years in Ephesus, his warning to the elders, and the letter he sends to Timothy, who stays on. Whether Paul or a later follower wrote 1 Timothy is debated, and the plan follows the letter's own account.

days.t: Savage wolves from your own number
Let no one despise your youth

plans.title: Leaders in the Church
plans.blurb: Elders, overseers and deacons: Paul's charge at Miletus, what 1 Timothy asks of leaders and how the church is to honor them. Some of the passages are debated.

days.t: Be shepherds of the church of God
If anyone aspires to be an overseer
Gifts for building up the body

plans.title: Money, Contentment and Generosity
plans.blurb: The rich fool, the secret of being content, and what 1 Timothy says about the love of money and about being rich in good works.

plans.title: Caring for Widows and Families
plans.blurb: The first widows in the church at Jerusalem and what 1 Timothy 5 says about families, widows and the church's part in caring for them.

days.t: The widows and the daily distribution
Honor the widows who are truly widows

plans.title: 2 Timothy in 4 Days
plans.blurb: The whole letter, one chapter a day: a prisoner's warm greeting, a call to be strong, warnings about the last days, and Paul's farewell.

days.t: Fan into flame the gift of God
I have fought the good fight

plans.title: 2 Timothy in 2 Days
plans.blurb: Two chapters a day through what is usually thought to be Paul's last letter.

days.t: Not ashamed, and strong in grace
The last days, Scripture and the final charge

plans.title: 2 Timothy in One Sitting
plans.blurb: All four chapters at once, about fifteen minutes. A letter from an older worker in chains to a younger friend he hopes to see before winter.

plans.title: Paul in Rome: His Last Letter
plans.blurb: Paul arrives in Rome as a prisoner in Acts, and 2 Timothy shows him in chains and expecting to die. Whether the letter describes a second imprisonment after Acts ends is an inference, and some scholars think a later writer used Paul's name.

plans.title: Scripture and the Man of God
plans.blurb: The Bereans who examined the Scriptures, Jesus opening the Scriptures on the Emmaus road, and Paul's words to Timothy that all Scripture is God-breathed.

days.t: He opened the Scriptures to them

plans.title: Faithful in Suffering
plans.blurb: Paul stoned at Lystra, a soldier and an athlete in 2 Timothy 2, joy in prison at Philippi, and the farewell of a man who has finished his course.

plans.title: The Last Days and False Teaching
plans.blurb: What Paul tells Timothy about people who turn away from sound teaching, set beside his earlier warnings. The passages are debated in places.

days.t: Terrible times in the last days

plans.title: The Life of Timothy
plans.blurb: Timothy joins Paul at Lystra, is sent to Thessalonica, is praised in Philippians, and receives Paul's last letter. His later life beyond the letters is not told in the Bible.

days.t: Like a son with a father
The faith of Lois and Eunice

plans.title: Titus in 3 Days
plans.blurb: The whole letter, one chapter a day: elders and rebellious teachers on Crete, life that fits sound teaching, and the kindness of God our Savior.

days.t: Left in Crete to set things in order
The grace of God has appeared
Washed, renewed and ready for good works

plans.title: Titus in One Sitting
plans.blurb: All three chapters at once, about ten minutes. A short letter from Paul to a coworker on Crete, who is to finish what Paul left undone.

plans.title: Paul and Crete
plans.blurb: Paul sails past Crete as a prisoner in Acts, and Titus 1 says he left Titus on the island. Whether the letter fits after Acts ends is an inference, and some scholars think a later writer used Paul's name.

days.t: The ship under the lee of Crete

plans.title: Grace That Saves and Teaches
plans.blurb: Saved by grace through faith in Ephesians, grace that trains believers to live well in Titus 2, and the kindness of God that appeared in Titus 3.

days.t: The grace of God has appeared
The kindness of God our Savior

plans.title: Elders in the Church
plans.blurb: Elders appointed at Lystra, Iconium and Antioch, the elders of Ephesus, and what Titus asks of the elders on Crete. Some of the passages are debated.

days.t: Be shepherds of the church of God

plans.title: A Life That Adorns the Gospel
plans.blurb: Paul's household instruction in Colossians 3, the same concern in Titus 2 for how outsiders see the gospel, and the call to be ready for every good work in Titus 3.

plans.title: Philemon in One Sitting
plans.blurb: The whole letter, about five minutes. Paul asks a slave owner to welcome back a slave who has become a brother.

plans.title: The Colossae Letters
plans.blurb: Colossians and Philemon were probably sent together, with Tychicus and Onesimus, to the same valley. Read the church letter, its closing greetings, then the private one.

days.t: Tychicus and Onesimus come with the letter
A slave who is now a brother

plans.title: Slave and Free in Christ
plans.blurb: Paul says there is neither slave nor free in Christ, gives household instruction to slaves and masters, and then writes one letter about one slave. The New Testament does not stop to say whether slavery should end; this plan lets you read the passages side by side.

days.t: Slaves and masters in the household

plans.title: Welcoming Someone Back
plans.blurb: A servant forgiven a large debt, a lost son welcomed home, a man forgiven and comforted in Corinth, and Paul's request to receive Onesimus. Four readings on mercy shown to someone who has done wrong.

days.t: The servant who would not forgive
The father who ran to meet his son
Receive him as you would receive me

plans.title: Paul in Chains
plans.blurb: Letters Paul writes as a prisoner: how his chains advanced the gospel in Philippians, his prayer for open doors in Colossians, his appeal in Philemon, and his last words from prison in 2 Timothy. Where he was held for each is debated.

days.t: My chains have advanced the gospel

plans.title: Hebrews in One Week
plans.blurb: The whole letter in seven readings: the Son greater than the angels, the warnings, the priest like Melchizedek, the new covenant, the one sacrifice, the roll call of faith and the closing exhortations.

days.t: God has spoken by his Son
Today, if you hear his voice
Maturity and the anchor of hope
A priest forever and a better covenant
By faith, and the race set before us

plans.title: Hebrews, One Chapter a Day
plans.blurb: All 13 chapters, one a day. Slow enough to follow the argument as it builds from the Son to the priest, the covenant, faith and endurance.

plans.title: Jesus, Our Great High Priest
plans.blurb: The priest who shares our weakness, the priest in the order of Melchizedek, and the priest who enters the heavenly sanctuary once for all. Read the five chapters that build the case.

days.t: Made like his brothers in every way
A great high priest who has passed through the heavens
Called by God, as Aaron was

plans.title: Faith from Abraham to the Cloud of Witnesses
plans.blurb: Paul on Abraham's faith in Romans and Galatians, then Hebrews 11, with its list of the faithful, and Hebrews 12, which turns the list into a call to run the race.

days.t: Those who have faith are sons of Abraham

plans.title: The Warnings of Hebrews
plans.blurb: The five warning passages, from drifting away to refusing the God who speaks. Some, especially Hebrews 6, are read in different ways by different Christians.

days.t: Do not throw away your confidence
Do not refuse him who speaks

plans.title: The New Covenant
plans.blurb: The cup at the Last Supper, Paul's ministry of the new covenant, and the long argument of Hebrews that the first covenant has been made obsolete by a better one.

days.t: This cup is the new covenant
Not of the letter but of the Spirit
Laws on the heart, sins remembered no more

plans.title: Entering God's Rest
plans.blurb: Jesus' invitation to the weary, the warning from the wilderness in Hebrews 3, and the Sabbath rest that remains for the people of God in Hebrews 4.

days.t: Come to me and I will give you rest

plans.title: James in One Week
plans.blurb: The whole letter in five readings, with two days to go back over it: trials and wisdom, doing the word, faith and works, the tongue and the two wisdoms, and patience and prayer.

days.t: No favoritism, and faith that works
The tongue and the wisdom from above
Passions, pride and the Lord's will

plans.title: James, One Chapter a Day
plans.blurb: All five chapters, one a day. A short, practical letter that rewards a slow reading.

plans.title: Faith and Works: James and Paul
plans.blurb: Paul on Abraham and justification by faith, James on faith that has no deeds, and Paul on faith working through love. Christians read the two letters together in different ways.

days.t: Saved by grace, created for good works

plans.title: The Tongue
plans.blurb: What James and the rest of Scripture say about speech: quick to listen, slow to speak, a small fire, and words that bless and curse.

days.t: Quick to listen, slow to speak
A small spark sets a forest ablaze
By your words you will be justified
Let no unwholesome word come out
Let your speech be seasoned with salt

plans.title: Wisdom from Above
plans.blurb: Asking God for wisdom, the two kinds of wisdom in James 3, and Paul's contrast between the wisdom of the world and the wisdom of God.

days.t: If any of you lacks wisdom
Wisdom that is pure, then peace-loving
The foolishness of God is wiser
In him are hidden all the treasures of wisdom

plans.title: The Poor and the Rich
plans.blurb: Jesus' blessings and woes, James on the gold ring and the unpaid wages, and Paul on the collection for the poor in Jerusalem.

days.t: Blessed are you who are poor
Has God not chosen the poor?

plans.title: Patience Under Trial
plans.blurb: Joy in trials, the farmer waiting for the rains, the example of Job, and Paul on suffering that produces endurance.

days.t: Be patient until the Lord's coming

plans.title: 1 Peter in One Week
plans.blurb: The whole letter in five readings, with two days to go back over it: hope and holiness, the living stone and the chosen people, households and the reason for hope, the fiery trial, and the flock and the Chief Shepherd.

days.t: A living hope, tested like gold
The living stone and the chosen people
Households, and the reason for your hope
Do not be surprised at the fiery trial
Shepherds, humility and the God of all grace

plans.title: 1 Peter, One Chapter a Day
plans.blurb: All five chapters, one a day. A letter to people under pressure, which rewards a slow reading.

plans.title: Suffering and Glory
plans.blurb: Peter's teaching on suffering for doing good, read beside Paul on suffering that produces endurance and affliction that is light and momentary.

days.t: A living hope, tested like gold
It is better to suffer for doing good
Do not be surprised at the fiery trial
Our affliction is light and momentary
The God of all grace will restore you

plans.title: Strangers and Exiles
plans.blurb: Believers as foreigners in the world: the heroes of faith who were strangers on the earth, Peter's exiles of the Dispersion, and Paul on a citizenship in heaven.

days.t: Strangers and exiles on the earth
A chosen people, foreigners in the world

plans.title: The Living Stone
plans.blurb: Jesus on the rock and the rejected stone, Peter on the living stone, and Paul on the cornerstone and the stone of stumbling.

days.t: On this rock I will build my church
A living stone, a spiritual house

plans.title: The Shepherd and the Flock
plans.blurb: The good shepherd, Jesus' words to Peter, Paul to the Ephesian elders, Peter to the elders, and the great Shepherd of the sheep.

days.t: The great Shepherd of the sheep

plans.title: Households in the Letters
plans.blurb: The teaching on wives, husbands, children, parents, slaves and masters in Ephesians, Colossians, Titus and 1 Peter, read side by side. Readers differ on how to apply it today.

days.t: Servants and the example of Christ
Wives and husbands: hope in God

plans.title: 2 Peter in One Week
plans.blurb: The whole letter in three readings, then back over each chapter and a last read through: everything for life and godliness, the false teachers and the God who rescues, and the Day of the Lord and the patience of God.

days.t: False teachers, and the God who rescues
The Day of the Lord, and God’s patience
The whole letter in one sitting

plans.title: 2 Peter, One Chapter a Day
plans.blurb: All three chapters, one a day. A short farewell letter, easy to read in one sitting, that is worth a second look.

plans.title: Growing in Godliness
plans.blurb: Peter’s chain of qualities, read beside the fruit of the Spirit, growing up into Christ, and growing in the knowledge of God.

days.t: Growing in the knowledge of God

plans.title: False Teachers and Warnings
plans.blurb: Jesus on false prophets, Paul to the Ephesian elders and to Timothy and Titus, Peter on false teachers who exploit with deceptive words, and Jude. Readers differ on who the teachers in 2 Peter were.

days.t: In later times some will abandon the faith

plans.title: The Day of the Lord
plans.blurb: The Day that comes like a thief: Jesus on keeping watch, Paul to the Thessalonians, Peter on the delay and the new heaven and earth, Hebrews on what cannot be shaken, and Revelation’s new creation.

days.t: Keep watch: the master of the house
The Day comes like a thief
The Lord is patient; a new heaven and earth
A kingdom that cannot be shaken
A new heaven and a new earth

plans.title: Farewell Words
plans.blurb: Jesus’ last teaching to his friends, Paul to the Ephesian elders, Paul’s last letter, and Peter’s reminder as he expects to lay his tent aside.

days.t: Do not let your hearts be troubled
I have fought the good fight

plans.title: The Holy Mountain
plans.blurb: The Transfiguration in Matthew, Mark and Luke, John on seeing his glory, and Peter looking back on the holy mountain as he writes.

days.t: His face shone like the sun
We were eyewitnesses of His majesty

plans.title: 1 John in One Week
plans.blurb: The whole letter in five readings, then back over the two chapters that carry its heart and a last read through: walking in the light, keeping the commandments, God is love, and the confidence that we have eternal life.

days.t: Fellowship, light and the cleansing blood
An advocate, a commandment and the antichrists
Children of God, and love in action
Test the spirits; God is love
Born of God; that you may know
Read the two chapters on love again
The whole letter in one sitting

plans.title: 1 John, One Chapter a Day
plans.blurb: All five chapters, one a day. A short letter that circles a few themes again and again, and gets clearer each time around.

plans.title: God Is Love, and We Love
plans.blurb: The new commandment in John, Paul on love that outlasts everything, nothing that can separate us, and John’s letter on a love that begins with God and shows itself in deed.

plans.title: Light and Darkness
plans.blurb: The light that shines in the darkness, from the Gospel of John to Ephesians, to the letter that says God is light, and to the city that needs no lamp.

days.t: The light shines in the darkness
I am the light of the world
The true light is already shining

plans.title: Abiding in Christ
plans.blurb: Jesus’ promise to remain with his friends, the vine and the branches, and John’s letter on remaining in Him and in love.

days.t: I will not leave you as orphans
Abide in Me, and I in you
He remains in us by the Spirit
Whoever abides in love abides in God

plans.title: Testing the Spirits
plans.blurb: How the New Testament tells true teaching from false: Jesus on false prophets, Paul on the Spirit and on testing everything, John on the confession of Jesus Christ come in the flesh, and Jude.

days.t: No one can say Jesus is Lord except by the Spirit

plans.title: Confession and Forgiveness
plans.blurb: Paul on sin and the gift, John’s promise that God is faithful and just to forgive, Hebrews on a sacrifice once for all, and James on confessing to one another.

days.t: All have sinned; a redemption in Christ
Confess your sins to one another

plans.title: Born of God
plans.blurb: The new birth in Jesus’ talk with Nicodemus, in Peter and Titus, and in John’s letter, which speaks of children of God who overcome the world.

days.t: Born again to a living hope
Everyone born of God overcomes the world

plans.title: The Gospel and the Letter: One Voice
plans.blurb: Chapters of the Gospel of John read next to the chapters of the letter that echo them: the beginning, the new commandment, abiding, and the reason it was all written.

days.t: In the beginning was the Word
An old commandment that is new

plans.title: 2 John in One Sitting
plans.blurb: Thirteen verses, about two minutes to read: a greeting, the old commandment to love, a warning about deceivers, a rule for the door, and a hope to talk face to face.

plans.title: 2 John in One Week
plans.blurb: The same short letter read once a day for a week, each day watching for one thing: the greeting, the walk, the deceivers, the teaching, the door, the closing, and then the whole again.

days.t: Read it through, and mark the word “truth”
Verses 4-6: walking, the commandment and love
Verses 8-9: watch yourselves, and remain in the teaching
Verses 10-11: the visitor at the door
Verses 12-13: paper and ink, and the greetings

plans.title: Truth and Love Together
plans.blurb: Jesus as the way, the truth and the life, Paul on speaking the truth in love and on a love that rejoices with the truth, then John’s two letters, where the two never come apart.

days.t: I am the way, the truth and the life

plans.title: The Commandment from the Beginning
plans.blurb: The new commandment Jesus gave at the supper, love as the fulfilling of the law, and the two letters of John that call it an old commandment that his readers have had from the beginning.

days.t: An old commandment that is new

plans.title: Deceivers and the Confession of Christ
plans.blurb: Jesus on those who come to deceive, Paul on a different gospel, Peter on false teachers, John on the confession that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh, and Jude on contending for the faith.

days.t: See that no one deceives you

plans.title: Remaining in the Teaching
plans.blurb: Paul’s charge to continue in what you have learned, Hebrews against being carried away by strange teachings, and John’s letters on staying in the teaching of Christ.

days.t: Continue in what you have learned
Let what you heard remain in you
Remaining in the teaching of Christ

plans.title: Hospitality and Its Limits
plans.blurb: Jesus on welcoming those he sends, Paul and Hebrews on opening the home to strangers, Peter on hospitality without complaint, and John on the guest who does not bring the teaching of Christ.

days.t: Do not neglect to show hospitality
Do not receive him into your home

plans.title: 3 John in One Sitting
plans.blurb: The shortest book in the New Testament, about two minutes to read: a prayer for a friend, thanks for his open door, a hard word about Diotrephes, a good word for Demetrius, and a hope to talk face to face.

plans.title: 3 John in One Week
plans.blurb: The same short letter read once a day for a week, each day watching one of its people or one of its lines, and then the whole again.

days.t: Read it through, and mark the word “truth”
Verses 1-4: Gaius, and no greater joy
Verses 5-8: the strangers and those who support them
Verses 9-10: Diotrephes, who loves to be first
Verses 13-14: pen and ink, peace, and the friends by name

plans.title: The Elder’s Two Notes
plans.blurb: 2 John and 3 John side by side over two days: one says whom not to welcome, the other praises a man who welcomes and blames a man who will not.

days.t: To the chosen lady: truth, love and the visitor at the door
To Gaius: the strangers, Diotrephes and Demetrius

plans.title: The Three Letters of John in a Week
plans.blurb: All seven chapters of John’s letters, one a day: the long first letter on light, love and life, and then the two short notes of the elder.

days.t: An old commandment that is new

plans.title: Welcoming the Stranger
plans.blurb: Jesus on receiving those he sends and on the stranger taken in, Lydia’s open house, Paul and Hebrews on hospitality, and Gaius, who was faithful to brothers he had never met.

days.t: I was a stranger and you took Me in
Lydia: come and stay at my house
Do not neglect hospitality to strangers
Faithful to the brothers, though they are strangers

plans.title: Who Wants to Be First?
plans.blurb: The disciples’ argument about greatness, the request of James and John, Jesus washing feet, the mind of Christ, Peter’s word to elders, and Diotrephes, who loved first place.

days.t: Last of all and servant of all
Not lording it over the flock
Diotrephes, who loves to be first

plans.title: Fellow Workers for the Truth
plans.blurb: People who never preached a sermon and still shared the work: the women who provided for Jesus, Priscilla and Aquila, Phoebe and the friends at Rome, the givers at Philippi, and Gaius.

days.t: The women who provided for them
We ought to support such men

plans.title: Imitate What Is Good
plans.blurb: Paul’s call to follow his example as he follows Christ, the model church at Thessalonica, the faith of leaders in Hebrews, and the elder’s word to Gaius between a bad example and a good one.

days.t: Imitate me, as I imitate Christ
You became imitators of us and of the Lord
Do not imitate what is evil, but what is good

plans.title: Jude in One Sitting
plans.blurb: Twenty-five verses, about four minutes to read: a call to contend for the faith, a sharp picture of people who twist grace, and one of the great closing prayers of the Bible.

plans.title: Jude in One Week
plans.blurb: The letter read through once a day for a week, each day slowing down on one part of it.

days.t: Read it through, and count the sets of three
Verses 1-4: called, loved, kept; contend for the faith
Verses 5-7: Egypt, the angels and Sodom
Verses 8-13: Michael, Cain, Balaam, Korah, and five pictures from nature
Verses 20-23: build, pray, keep, wait, and show mercy
Verses 24-25: to Him who is able to keep you

plans.title: Jude and 2 Peter Side by Side
plans.blurb: Jude 4-18 and 2 Peter 2 run alongside each other: the angels, Sodom, Balaam, the waterless clouds and the scoffers. Three days to read them together and see what each keeps and what each leaves out.

days.t: 2 Peter 2: the same warnings, with Noah and Lot rescued
The scoffers, and how each letter ends

plans.title: The Brothers of Jesus
plans.blurb: From the family that thought Jesus was out of his mind to James and Jude, who called themselves his servants: the story of the Lord’s brothers across the New Testament.

days.t: His family comes to take charge of Him
Even His own brothers did not believe
With the believers in the upper room
James, a servant of the Lord Jesus Christ
Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and a brother of James

plans.title: Contend for the Faith
plans.blurb: Paul’s warning to the elders of Ephesus, his fight for the gospel in Galatia, his charge to Timothy and Titus, and Jude’s call to hold on to the faith handed down once for all.

days.t: Savage wolves will come in among you
Fight the good fight of the faith
Preach the word; I have kept the faith
Holding firmly to the trustworthy word
The faith entrusted once for all to the saints

plans.title: Grace Is Not a License
plans.blurb: Jude’s intruders turned the grace of God into an excuse for sin. Paul, Peter and John all answer the same idea.

days.t: Shall we sin so that grace may increase?
Freedom, but not for the flesh
Grace trains us to say no to ungodliness
Free, but not as a cover for evil
No one born of God keeps on sinning
They turn the grace of our God into a license

plans.title: Kept by God
plans.blurb: Jude begins with people who are kept and ends with the God who is able to keep them. Five other chapters on the same promise, and then Jude.

days.t: No one will snatch them out of My hand
Holy Father, keep them in Your name
Nothing can separate us from the love of God
He who began a good work will finish it
Shielded by God’s power through faith
Kept in Jesus Christ; keep yourselves; He is able to keep you

plans.title: The Great Doxologies
plans.blurb: Short hymns of praise that close a letter or break into the middle of one, from Romans to Revelation, ending with Jude’s.

days.t: From Him and through Him and to Him are all things
To Him who is able to strengthen you
To Him who is able to do far more than we ask
To the King eternal, immortal, invisible
The God of peace equip you
To the only God our Savior be glory

plans.title: Revelation One Chapter a Day
plans.blurb: The whole book in twenty-two days, one chapter at a time: the letters to the seven churches, the throne and the Lamb, the seals, trumpets and bowls, the fall of Babylon, and the new Jerusalem.

days.t: John on Patmos sees the risen Christ
The sealed servants and the great multitude
Silence in heaven; the first four trumpets
The angel and the little scroll
The two witnesses and the seventh trumpet
The Lamb on Mount Zion and the harvest
The song of Moses and of the Lamb
The woman on the scarlet beast
Hallelujah, and the rider on the white horse
The thousand years and the great white throne
A new heaven and a new earth
The river of life, and Come, Lord Jesus

plans.title: Revelation in One Week
plans.blurb: Read the book in seven sittings, about the way it was first heard: aloud and in large pieces, so the patterns and repeated songs stand out.

days.t: The risen Christ and the seven churches
The seals, and the people sealed by God
The trumpets and the two witnesses
The dragon, the beasts and the Lamb
The bowls and the fall of Babylon
The return of Christ and the new creation

plans.title: The Seven Letters
plans.blurb: Eight days with Revelation 1-3: the vision of Christ among the lampstands, then one church a day. Each letter has praise, warning and a promise to the one who overcomes.

days.t: One like the Son of Man among the lampstands
Ephesus: the love you had at first
Pergamum: where Satan has his throne
Laodicea: I stand at the door and knock

plans.title: The Worship of Heaven
plans.blurb: Revelation is full of songs. Six days with the scenes of worship around the throne, from Holy, Holy, Holy to the Hallelujahs of chapter 19.

days.t: The kingdom of the world has become His
Great and wonderful are Your works

plans.title: The Lamb
plans.blurb: From John the Baptist’s cry by the Jordan to the throne of God and of the Lamb: the New Testament’s picture of Jesus as the sacrificed and living Lamb.

days.t: A lamb without blemish or spot
A Lamb who appeared to have been slain
The Lamb will be their shepherd
They follow the Lamb wherever He goes
The marriage supper of the Lamb
The throne of God and of the Lamb

plans.title: Hope for Hard Times
plans.blurb: Revelation was written to churches under pressure. Seven passages for anyone who is suffering or afraid, from the risen Christ who holds the keys of death to the God who wipes away every tear.

days.t: Do not be afraid; I hold the keys
Be faithful, and I will give you the crown of life
God will wipe away every tear
They conquered by the blood of the Lamb
Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord
No more death or mourning or crying or pain

plans.title: Two Cities: Babylon and the New Jerusalem
plans.blurb: Revelation ends with two cities, each pictured as a woman: the great prostitute Babylon and the bride of the Lamb. Five days reading them side by side.

days.t: The woman on the scarlet beast
Come out of her, My people
The bride has made herself ready
The holy city coming down from God
The river and the tree of life

plans.title: The Return of Christ
plans.blurb: What the New Testament says about the coming of Christ, from the words of Jesus on the Mount of Olives to the last prayer of the Bible, Come, Lord Jesus.

days.t: The coming of the Son of Man
He will come back in the same way
We will be with the Lord forever
The rider on the white horse

plans.title: All Things New
plans.blurb: The New Testament’s hope is not escape from the world but a world made new. Six days from Paul’s groaning creation to the new heaven and new earth.

days.t: Creation waits to be set free
New heavens and a new earth
Behold, I make all things new

plans.title: Jesus in Revelation and the Gospels
plans.blurb: The Jesus of Revelation is the Jesus of the Gospels: the Son of Man, the Lamb, the Word, the Shepherd, the one who knocks. Six days pairing them.

days.t: The Son of Man coming with the clouds
The cup and the marriage supper
